return { irq: irq ?? null, queue: rest };

steps.explain: The first interrupt is the most urgent, because `enqueue` keeps the queue sorted.
Hand it back with the rest of the queue. An empty queue gives `null`.

should-preempt.code: return core.phase === "FETCH" && !inHandler(core) && core.retired >= scheduler.quantum && pickNext(scheduler) !== undefined;

steps.explain: Switch a program out only when all four hold: the core is between instructions (`FETCH`), it isn't in an interrupt handler, the program has run its quantum of instructions, and another program is waiting for a turn.
